about.intro: 我是亓炳堃，一名国际学校理科教师，教授物理、数学与高等数学。
paragraphs: 我的学习与研究经历跨越复旦大学、纽约市立大学、北京大学和洛桑联邦理工学院，研究兴趣集中在非厄米光子学。我也已获得亚利桑那州立大学的 Master of Engineering, Computing and Technology 学位。
从物理研究到课堂教学，我一直喜欢把复杂问题拆解成可以理解、可以尝试的步骤。现在，我也在探索用 AI 辅助开发教学工具，将备课中的具体需求做成可使用的题库与练习网站。

case.label: 学习工具 / ESAT PRACTICE
case.title: 从一次作答，走向下一次练习。
cards: 学习问题
知道答对或答错之后，还需要看清解题思路，并找到值得继续练习的内容。
练习方式
按知识点开始练习，或进入同一科目的随机组卷与系列模考。
回顾线索
把错题与主考点的作答情况放在一起看，为下一轮练习选择一个具体目标。
steps: 选择并作答
从科目或知识点进入练习，先完成自己的判断，再提交答案并查看反馈。
读解析，回看思路
打开已提供的解析，对照关键关系和计算步骤；回到错题本时，再看自己当时的选择。
看主考点，再练一次
在统计页查看各主考点的作答情况，选择需要继续练习的内容，通过“练这个”进入对应题目。

case.label: 案例 / 从接线到图线
case.title: 亲手完成测量，让数据给出电阻。
cards: 教学问题
公式 U = IR 很简洁，但理解一次测量还需要正确接线、读表并比较多组数据。
设计选择
用三维实验台组织器材，再提供清楚的双表视图。读数由使用者手动记录，可逐行更正。

virtual-lab-measurement.jpg

将电流表串联、电压表并联到待测电阻两端，检查滑动变阻器接法并选择合适量程。

projects.kicker: 教学设计 · 原创课例 · 45 分钟计划
projects.summary: 一节面向已有 IGCSE 基础学生的受力分析课：先暴露常见误解，再通过示范、独立作答与退出题检查理解。
features: 英文学生题纸与独立解答，先尝试再核对
自绘受力图，明确研究对象、外力和正方向
中文教师教案，配有追问、纠错提示和分项评分
从同一模型迁移到拉力撤去、竖直运动与第三定律
story: 学生会代入 F = ma，并不一定能判断该把哪些力放进方程。我把这节课的重点放在建模：先选定研究对象，只画作用在它身上的真实外力，再选正方向、列方程并解释结果。
题纸从“匀速是否需要合力”与第三定律力对开始，接着比较撤去拉力前后的箱子，再用悬挂物和退出题检查迁移。教师教案明确了何时示范、何时让学生独立完成，以及如何根据错误回到相应步骤。

case.label: 课例 / 诊断、建模与反馈
case.title: 从受力图到能解释的答案
cards: 教学目标
把研究对象、真实外力与正方向说清楚，再把图、方程和解释连起来。
学习材料
英文学生题纸、独立解答和中文教师教案，保留完整的课堂练习流程。
反馈设计
保留第一次判断，让学生说明一次订正，再用新的退出题情境检查迁移。
images: teaching/forces-before-after.svg
同一个物体，条件改变后要重新检查力的来源。箭头为示意，不按大小比例绘制。
steps: 先诊断，留下理由
0–5 分钟 · 用两道短问区分匀速与零合力、平衡力与第三定律力对。保留第一次回答，作为后续反馈的起点。
把受力画清楚
5–18 分钟 · 选定一个物体，逐一标出外力和正方向。以水平拉箱为示范，把图、方程与加速度方向连在一起。
换情境，再解释
18–45 分钟 · 独立完成撤去拉力与悬挂物任务，说明一次订正的理由，再用退出题检查能否迁移到新情境。

teachingExample.eyebrow: 10 分钟 · 互动教学示例
teachingExample.title: 波的叠加：先预测，再观察，最后推导
teachingExample.intro: 两列振幅都是 1 的波相遇，合振幅一定是 2 吗？先给出自己的判断，再用波形与数学检查。这个自学示例展示我如何把直觉、观察和推导连接起来。
teachingExample.duration: 预测 2 分钟 · 观察 3 分钟 · 推导 3 分钟 · 挑战 2 分钟
teachingExample.learningGoal: 区分瞬时位移与振幅，说明相位差如何改变合振幅，并用一个公式检验观察。
assumptions: 考虑满足线性叠加原理的两列简谐波；在同一位置、同一时刻，沿同一方向测量的位移可以直接相加。
两列波的频率相同，相位差 φ 固定。本演示还取相同波长和相同传播方向，因此相位差不随位置改变。
第一列波的振幅 A₁ 固定为 1；第二列的振幅 A₂ 可在 0 到 1 之间调节。所有位移和振幅都使用相同的相对单位。

steps.title: 预测：先留下一个判断
steps.text: 先不看合振幅读数。令 A₁ = A₂ = 1，预测相位差 φ 分别为 0°、90°、180° 时的合振幅 R。写下一个数值或范围，并说明理由。
prompts: 两列波的波峰会在同一位置出现吗？
如果某一时刻合位移为 0，是否就说明合振幅为 0？

steps.title: 观察：逐点相加，而非只看波峰
steps.text: 在下面的实验中，将第二列波的振幅设为 1，依次把相位差调到 0°、90°、180°。暂停动画，在同一个横坐标读取两条曲线的位移，检查亮色合成曲线是否等于它们的代数和，再核对合振幅读数。
prompts: φ = 90° 时，在第一列波波峰的位置，合位移为 1；但合成波的最大位移是否也只有 1？
播放动画并观察一个固定位置：瞬时位移随时间改变，合振幅在当前设置下保持不变。

steps.title: 推导：把观察写成一个公式
steps.text: 令 θ = kx − ωt。先相加位移，再展开三角函数：
equations: y₁ = A₁ sin θ，y₂ = A₂ sin(θ + φ)
y = y₁ + y₂ = (A₁ + A₂ cos φ) sin θ + A₂ sin φ cos θ
R² = (A₁ + A₂ cos φ)² + (A₂ sin φ)²
prompts: 将 sin θ 和 cos θ 的系数与 R sin(θ + δ) 的展开式比较，再平方相加，消去 δ。
公式给出的是合振幅 R，不是某个位置、某个时刻的位移 y。完全抵消时 R = 0，合成波的相位 δ 无需定义。

challenge.title: 挑战：反相就一定完全抵消吗？
challenge.question: 保持 A₁ = 1，把 A₂ 调为 0.50，相位差设为 180°。先计算 R，再拖动滑块验证。解释为什么反相不再得到一条零位移直线。
challenge.extension: 不做逐一试算：当 A₁ = 1、A₂ = 0.50 时，随相位差改变，R 的最小值和最大值分别是多少？

answers.label: 同相 · φ = 0°
answers.text: R = 2。两列波在每个位置的位移同号，且波峰相遇。

answers.label: 相差四分之一周期 · φ = 90°
answers.text: R = √2 ≈ 1.41。合成波的峰值不在任一原波峰值的位置，因此不能只在第一列波的波峰处读取振幅。

answers.label: 等振幅反相 · φ = 180°
answers.text: R = 0。两列波在每个位置、每个时刻的位移大小相等、方向相反。

answers.label: 挑战 · A₂ = 0.50，φ = 180°
answers.text: R = |1 − 0.50| = 0.50。反相使位移相减；只有振幅也相等时才能完全抵消。

answers.label: 拓展
answers.text: 0.50 ≤ R ≤ 1.50。一般地，|A₁ − A₂| ≤ R ≤ A₁ + A₂。

teachingExample.keyDistinction: 叠加原理相加的是同一位置、同一时刻的带符号位移：y = y₁ + y₂。振幅是振动偏离平衡位置的最大距离，不能一般地写成 R = A₁ + A₂；本例只有同相时才成立。
teachingExample.teachingTip: 先保留预测及理由，再一次只改变一个参数。出现不一致时，先在同一横坐标读出三个位移，再讨论振幅。最后用不等振幅的反例检查“反相就完全抵消”这一判断，而不只检查是否会代入公式。

about.intro: I'm Bingkun Qi, a science teacher at an international school, teaching physics, mathematics and advanced mathematics.
paragraphs: My studies and research have taken me to Fudan University, CUNY, Peking University and EPFL, with a research focus on non-Hermitian photonics. I also hold a Master of Engineering, Computing and Technology from Arizona State University.

From physics research to the classroom, I enjoy breaking complex problems into steps that people can understand and explore. I am also experimenting with AI-assisted development, turning everyday teaching needs into question banks and practice websites.

projects.title: From a force diagram to an explanation
projects.summary: A force-analysis lesson for students with an IGCSE foundation: uncover a misconception, build a model, then check understanding through independent practice and an exit ticket.
features: An English worksheet with separate solutions: attempt first, check afterwards
Original force diagrams that make the object, external forces and positive direction explicit
A Chinese teacher plan with prompts, feedback cues and marking guidance
Transfer from one model to a released rope, vertical motion and Newton’s third law
story: Substituting into F = ma does not by itself show that a student knows which forces belong in the equation. This lesson starts with modelling: choose the object, draw the external forces acting on it, define a positive direction, then write and interpret the equation.

Short questions on constant velocity and third-law pairs lead into a worked crate example. Students then compare the forces before and after a rope is released, apply the model to a suspended load, and attempt an exit ticket independently. The teacher plan specifies when to model, when to step back, and how to use an error to revisit the relevant step.

case.title: From a force diagram to an explanation
cards: The learning goal
Identify the object, external forces and positive direction, then connect the diagram, equation and explanation.
The learning materials
An English worksheet, separate solutions and a Chinese teacher plan preserve the full classroom-practice sequence.
Feedback by design

steps: Diagnose and keep the reasoning
Minutes 0–5 · Two short questions separate constant velocity from resultant force, and balanced forces from a third-law pair. Keep the first response as a starting point for feedback.
Make the force model explicit
Minutes 5–18 · Choose one object, identify its external forces and set a positive direction. A pulled crate connects the diagram, the equation and the direction of acceleration.
Transfer, explain and check
Minutes 18–45 · Students work independently on a released rope and a suspended load, explain a correction, then use a new exit-ticket situation to check transfer.

teachingExample.title: Wave superposition: predict, observe, then derive
teachingExample.intro: When two waves each have an amplitude of 1, must the resultant amplitude be 2? Make a prediction, then test it with a graph and a short derivation. This self-study example connects intuition, observation and mathematics.
teachingExample.duration: Predict 2 min · Observe 3 min · Derive 3 min · Challenge 2 min
teachingExample.learningGoal: Distinguish instantaneous displacement from amplitude, explain the effect of phase difference, and check an observation with an equation.
assumptions: We consider two sinusoidal waves obeying linear superposition. Their displacements, measured along the same direction at the same position and time, add algebraically.
The waves have the same frequency and a fixed phase difference φ. This demonstration also uses the same wavelength and direction of travel, so φ is independent of position.
The amplitude of wave 1 is fixed at A₁ = 1. A₂ can vary from 0 to 1. All displacements and amplitudes use the same relative units.

steps.title: Predict: commit to an explanation
steps.text: Before looking at the resultant-amplitude readout, set A₁ = A₂ = 1 in your model. Predict R for phase differences of 0°, 90° and 180°. Record a number or a range, with a reason.
prompts: Will the crests of both waves occur at the same position?
If the resultant displacement is zero at one instant, must its amplitude be zero?

steps.title: Observe: add point by point
steps.text: In the lab below, set the amplitude of wave 2 to 1, then move the phase slider to 0°, 90° and 180°. Pause the animation. At one horizontal coordinate, read the two displacements and check that the bright resultant curve equals their algebraic sum. Then check the resultant amplitude.
prompts: At φ = 90°, the resultant displacement is 1 at a crest of wave 1. Is that also the maximum displacement of the resultant?
Play the animation and watch one fixed position: instantaneous displacement changes with time, while the amplitude stays constant for the current settings.

steps.title: Derive: express the pattern mathematically
steps.text: Let θ = kx − ωt. Add the displacements, then expand the trigonometric expression:
equations: y₁ = A₁ sin θ; y₂ = A₂ sin(θ + φ)
y = y₁ + y₂ = (A₁ + A₂ cos φ) sin θ + A₂ sin φ cos θ
R² = (A₁ + A₂ cos φ)² + (A₂ sin φ)²
prompts: Match the coefficients of sin θ and cos θ with the expansion of R sin(θ + δ). Square and add to eliminate δ.
The formula gives the amplitude R, not the displacement y at a particular position and time. When R = 0, the phase δ of the zero resultant need not be defined.

challenge.title: Challenge: do opposite phases always cancel?
challenge.question: Keep A₁ = 1, set A₂ = 0.50 and φ = 180°. Calculate R before testing it with the sliders. Explain why the resultant is no longer a line of zero displacement.
challenge.extension: Without testing every setting, find the minimum and maximum R as the phase varies with A₁ = 1 and A₂ = 0.50.

answers.label: In phase · φ = 0°
answers.text: R = 2. The displacements have the same sign at each position, and the crests coincide.

answers.label: A quarter cycle apart · φ = 90°
answers.text: R = √2 ≈ 1.41. The resultant reaches its peak at a different position from either individual wave, so reading the displacement at a crest of wave 1 does not give the resultant amplitude.

answers.label: Equal amplitudes, opposite phase · φ = 180°
answers.text: R = 0. At every position and time, the displacements have equal magnitudes and opposite signs.

answers.label: Challenge · A₂ = 0.50, φ = 180°
answers.text: R = |1 − 0.50| = 0.50. Opposite phases make the displacements subtract; complete cancellation also requires equal amplitudes.

answers.label: Extension
answers.text: 0.50 ≤ R ≤ 1.50. In general, |A₁ − A₂| ≤ R ≤ A₁ + A₂.

teachingExample.keyDistinction: Superposition adds signed displacements at the same position and time: y = y₁ + y₂. Amplitude is the maximum distance from equilibrium. In general, R is not A₁ + A₂; in this model that equality holds when the waves are in phase.
teachingExample.teachingTip: Keep the original prediction and reasoning, then vary one parameter at a time. When observations disagree with a prediction, read all three displacements at the same horizontal coordinate before discussing amplitude. Use unequal amplitudes to test the claim that opposite phases always cancel, as well as the ability to substitute into a formula.
teachingExample.handoutNote: Two pages, one per language, with a recording table and answers.
teachingExample.scopeNote: This is a public teaching example; it contains no student records or claims of measured classroom outcomes.

explainers.title: Shaping light with gain and loss
explainers.question: How does amplification or absorption reshape a lattice mode?
explainers.why: It offers another design parameter for controlling localization.
explainers.finding: In the studied lattices, non-Hermitian particle-hole symmetry creates a flat real spectrum. Stronger gain/loss increasingly localizes an edge-defect mode. Zero is measured relative to a reference frequency.
explainers.credit: Bingkun Qi is the first author.

explainers.title: Anchoring a zero mode at the boundary
explainers.question: Can a mode retain its reference frequency without global symmetry?
explainers.why: This suggests another route to frequency-stable photonic devices.
explainers.finding: Coupling a boundary zero mode to the bulk under specific non-Hermitian conditions yields a zero mode robust to bulk disorder. The boundary and coupling conditions must remain satisfied.
explainers.credit: Bingkun Qi is a co-author, listed third.
